To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hydrogen bonds between the hydrophilic and hydrophobic blocks of LCBCs lead to the formation of a lamellar structure inside the hydrophilic nanocylinders upon self-assembly.

the introduction of urethane groups in LCBCs induces hydrogen bonds with ether groups of PEO blocks, leading to imperfect crystalization of the P EO block and the formation of a lamellar structure inside PEO nanocylinder.

hydrogen-bond-induced microphase separation of LCBCs leads to the formation of hierarchically assembled sub-10 nm nanocylinders, which is a new strategy to fabricate sub-10 nm nanostructures without any dopants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication of hierarchal self-assembly of LCBCs through hydrogen bonding interactions.
the synthesis of a novel series of LCBCs containing urethane groups in their side chain, which are capable of forming hydrogen bonds with the ether groups in the PEO block.

the fabrication and characterization of hierarchical self-assembled sub 10 nm microstructures of amphiphillic LCBCs with the existence of hydrogen bonding between the hydrophobic and the hydrophilic blocks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hydrogen bonds are an effective way to induce hierarchical self-assembly of LCBCs.
hydrogen bonding between the urethane groups and ether groups of PEO induces hierarchical self-assembly in LCBCs.
hydrogen bonds are able to induce hierarchical self-assembly of LCBCs without any additives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hydrogen bond between urethane groups and ether groups in PEO is strong enough to induce the self-assembly of LCBCs into hierarchical sub-10 nm morphologies.
the hydrogen bonds between the urethane groups and ether groups in the PEO blocks are the driving force to form the hierarchically self-assembly structures of sub-10-nm microstructures.
we have developed an efficient method to fabricate sub-10 nm hierarchical structures in LCBCs through hydrogen-bond-induced microphase separation without any dopants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hydrogen bond between the side chain of LCBCs and the PEO block can induce the hierarchical microphase-separated structures.
hydrogen-bond-induced crystallization in LCBCs can be utilized to fabricate sub-10 nm hierarchical microphase-separated structures without any additives.
hydrogen bonds can be utilized to induce the formation of hierarchical microstructures of LCBCs.
